d: An interior view of the ancient castle of Langres, or ancient Lingona in which I believed Sabino died. On one side fenced with thick, and solitary cypresses. On the other wall, and towers destroyed, all leftovers of fire, and ruins. Among these I glimpsed a temple dedicated to Mercury, ancient deity of the Gauls, under which is the underground of Sabino, to which one passes through an unknown path, and hidden among the ruins. Next to the temple there was the Mausoleum raised by Epponina to his spouse Sabino. Sabino, alone, in Arminius.
Interior of a magnificent pavilion, which occupies the whole scene, next to which I glimpsed encamped the Roman army. Annio, and Tito with sheet in hand.
Interior view of the ancient castle of Langres, or Lingona. Epponina, in the Sabino.
Sabino, and Epponina, who follows him.
Escape of rooms. Annio, ind Voadice.
Lonely part of a garden. Sabino, then Arminio.
Epponina, Annio, Sabino, Indi Tito con Guardie.
Interior view of the castle of Langres. Night. Sabino, and Arminio.
Tito, and Annio, followed by Soldiers with faces.
Underground faces, supported by a colonnade half devastated by time, to which you go down a large staircase. Sabino, at Titus, and Annio with guards with faces on, then Epponina.
Epponina and Tito, then Annio with Sabino chained between Guards.
A gloomy room destined for the torture of Sabin. Sabin, and Custodi, who, at the sound of a gloomy march, is led to the torture.
Epponina, between the Guards, and said.
A sound of joyful symphony changes the scene into an illuminated royal hall, and full of People. Titus with the sons of Sabino, Voadice, Arminius, Annius, and sayings.
